attribution.note: Marcus recounts and reaffirms his own argument.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the firm prediction and asserted necessity of a new paradigm. No deadline or conditional antecedent is stated.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. AGI criteria and the boundary of a paradigm change require interpretation beyond Marcus's words; the contract appropriately requires capability and architectural evidence.

evidence.note: The dated independent benchmark shows substantial progress on unfamiliar tasks, but establishes neither broad AGI nor the required architectural criterion.
The pre-cutoff assessment finds public AGI evidence insufficient. That does not establish an inherent LLM limitation or the necessity of a new paradigm. Company-reported scores remain disclosures.
The pre-cutoff preprint reports embodied capabilities and deployment limitations. Neither establishes AGI or a permanent limitation of the relevant LLM approach.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and neither early-resolution condition is met. Benchmark and embodied progress do not establish AGI within the relevant paradigm. Current limitations and insufficient evidence of AGI do not establish that a paradigm change is necessary.
